# viz

> viz is a free collection of 117 interactive, in-browser visualizations of the math inside neural networks: attention, KV caches, state-space scans, convolution, mixture-of-experts routing, normalization, quantization, diffusion sampling and more. Each page shows the linear algebra of one mechanism, step by step, with live controls.

Start at https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ (all demos) or https://viz.math.gaema.ai/tour.html (a guided tour). The demos run in the browser and need JavaScript; each page also carries its explanation as plain HTML, and each line below says what one of them shows. Content is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Part of gaema (https://gaema.ai/llms.txt).

## A — Foundational primitives

- [matmul: C = A · B (the GEMM atom)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/matmul/): Every output cell is one row·column dot product, and every layer of every model reduces to this. Watch the tiles light up, then resize the problem and watch the cost grow.
- [dot-product: a · b (projection + cosine)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/dot-product/): Two vectors multiplied term by term, plus the geometry behind it: the projection of one onto the other, the angle between them, and the cosine similarity attention is built on.
- [dtype-bits: the numeric zoo, bit by bit](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/dtype-bits/): Twenty-three number formats bit by bit: sign, exponent and mantissa, what each can represent, and the rounding error you accept for the bits you save. Plus which hardware runs which.
- [softmax: logits → probabilities](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/softmax/): Scores become probabilities: exponentiate, then normalise. Temperature sharpens or flattens the result, and subtracting the largest value first is what stops it overflowing.

## B — Attention

- [qkv-projection: one embedding → Q, K, V](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/qkv-projection/): One token embedding becomes three different views of itself — a query, a key and a value — through three separate weight matrices. Everything attention does begins here.
- [scaled-dot-attention: the single-head pipeline](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/scaled-dot-attention/): The full single-head pipeline: compare every query to every key, scale by the square root of the dimension, mask, softmax, then mix the values. Every other page varies this.
- [QK-norm: a long key stops winning by being long](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/qk-norm/): Queries and keys are divided by their own RMS before the dot product. A long key then stops winning the softmax just by being long, and the aligned key can take the mass.
- [multi-head: split into heads, attend in parallel, concat](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/multi-head/): Split the embedding into heads, run attention independently in each, then concatenate and project. Each head is free to learn a different relationship between tokens.
- [gqa-mqa: KV-head sharing (MHA / GQA / MQA)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/gqa-mqa/): Several query heads share one set of keys and values. The cache shrinks by the sharing factor, which is why generation gets cheaper — and head-specific detail is what you give up.
- [cross-layer KV: later layers reuse an earlier cache](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/cross-layer-kv/): Every share-th layer writes keys and values, and the tail still gets a writer. The layers until the next writer reuse that cache. A share of 1 means every layer writes its own cache.
- [causal-mask: why decode only attends to the past](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/causal-mask/): Blank out everything above the diagonal so a token can only read what came before it. Remove the mask and watch information leak backwards from tokens not yet written.
- [fill-in-the-middle: the middle can see the ending](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/fill-in-the-middle/): The tokens run prefix, then suffix, then the missing middle, so a causal mask lets the middle read the ending. Two examples under that mask let the second read the first. Isolate them and those cross pairs drop to 0.
- [attention-patterns: full / sliding-window / hybrid / sink](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/attention-patterns/): Full, sliding-window, hybrid and sink patterns side by side: which past tokens each query may read, and how much of the sequence each choice quietly throws away.
- [kv-cache: the KV cache during decode](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-cache/): The cache gains one column per generated token, per layer, and never shrinks. This is why generation is fast, and why a long chat runs out of memory before it runs out of words.
- [rope: rotary position embedding (per-pair 2-D rotation)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/rope/): Position is encoded by rotating each pair of dimensions by an angle proportional to position. Relative position falls out of the arithmetic; stretching the angles extends context.
- [flash-attention: tiled online softmax (never materialize N×N)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/flash-attention/): Attention computed tile by tile with a running maximum and sum, so the full score matrix is never stored. Same answer, memory that grows with the tile instead of the sequence.
- [sparse-attention-select: choosing what to attend to](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/sparse-attention-select/): A cheap scorer ranks every past token and only the top few get real attention. Drag the cut and watch the selected set move — and a needle just outside it contribute nothing.
- [attention-sinks: the position everything attends to and nothing reads](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/attention-sinks/): Softmax has to put its weight somewhere, so a head with nothing to look at dumps it on the first token. Huge attention, almost no contribution — and deleting it breaks the model.
- [sage attention: low-precision scores](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/sage-attention/): The attention scores are rounded to eight-bit integers before the softmax. The output moves, and a row of zeros stays exact because it was already on the grid.

## C — Transformer block

- [tokenization: Byte-Pair Encoding builds the vocab](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/tokenization/): Byte-pair encoding builds a vocabulary by repeatedly merging the commonest adjacent pair. Watch text become token ids, and see why an unusual word costs several of them.
- [embedding: token-id → row lookup (and the tied lm_head)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/embedding/): A token id is a row number, so the embedding table is looked up rather than multiplied. Tied and untied output weights are the same table read in two directions.
- [mlp-gated: the SwiGLU / GeGLU feed-forward block](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/mlp-gated/): Two projections up, one gate, one projection back down. The gate multiplies element by element, letting the layer suppress its own features — and this is where most parameters live.
- [activations: GELU (erf / tanh) vs SiLU/Swish vs Mish](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/activations/): GeLU, SiLU, Mish and their cheap approximations on one axis. They differ mostly near zero, and that small difference is what decides how gradients flow through a deep stack.
- [normalization: RMSNorm vs LayerNorm (and pre/post-norm)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/normalization/): RMSNorm against LayerNorm: per-row statistics with and without subtracting the mean, and why placing the step before or after the block changes how stably it trains.
- [residual-stream: the residual highway](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/residual-stream/): Every block reads the stream, adds its contribution and writes it back. Nothing is ever replaced, which is why information from the first layer can still reach the last.
- [lm-head: hidden state → vocab logits](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/lm-head/): The final projection turns one hidden vector into a score for every vocabulary entry. It is frequently the same matrix as the embedding table, read the other way round.
- [transformer-block: one full pre-norm block](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/transformer-block/): The whole block assembled: normalise, attend, add, normalise, feed forward, add. Step it and watch one residual stream get transformed, then handed to an identical block.
- [prefill-vs-decode: two inference regimes](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/prefill-vs-decode/): Two different regimes: reading the prompt is one large parallel matrix multiply, writing the reply is a long series of tiny ones. One is compute-bound, the other memory-bound.
- [sampling: greedy / top-k / top-p / temperature](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/sampling/): Greedy, temperature, top-k and top-p applied to the same distribution. Watch which words survive each filter, and how abruptly the tail gets cut away as you tighten it.
- [hyper-connections: the residual highway, widened](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/hyper-connections/): Several parallel residual streams instead of one, with learned weights deciding which a block reads, which it writes, and how they mix. At one stream it is exactly the classic residual.
- [sequence-packing: many documents, one row](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/sequence-packing/): Several documents share one row. A block-diagonal mask keeps them apart. A mask that is true everywhere still trains, and tokens read across the document boundary.

## D — Mixture of Experts

- [moe-routing: router, top-k experts, load balancing](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/moe-routing/): A router scores every expert for every token and sends each token to the best few. Watch the load land unevenly, and watch tokens get dropped when an expert fills up.
- [moe-balance: load balancing, collapse, and why experts starve](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/moe-balance/): Two routes. Auxiliary-loss mode mixes a skewed router toward uniform as lambda rises from 0 to 1. Selection-bias mode offsets scores only to choose the top-k; the combine weight is the softmax of the raw selected scores and the auxiliary weight is 0. In bias mode both compare panes are that route.
- [per-token-compute: not every token needs the same amount of work](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/per-token-compute/): Easy tokens leave early, hard ones go round again, so the compute profile is ragged rather than rectangular. GPUs want uniform work, and the padding can cost more than the saving.
- [expert-placement: which GPU an expert lives on](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/expert-placement/): Which GPU an expert lives on, which is a different question from which expert a token picks. Placement decides what crosses the interconnect, and one hot expert alone sets the step time.

## E — Non-transformer sequence (SSM)

- [ssm-scan: the selective state-space scan (Mamba / S6)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ssm-scan/): A recurrent state swept along the sequence, where an input-dependent step size decides what to keep and what to forget. Constant memory per token, however long the sequence runs.
- [mamba-block: the full Mamba block](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/mamba-block/): The complete block: project in, short convolution, gate, selective scan, gate again, project out. The scan is the only part that carries information along the sequence.
- [gated-deltanet: the linear-attention delta-rule state update](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/gated-deltanet/): Memory as a fixed-size matrix rather than a growing cache: a decay gate fades what is already stored, and a delta rule writes the new key-value pair over the top of it.
- [delta-rule-gates: how the gate in a delta rule became two gates](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/delta-rule-gates/): One recurrence, three gates: a single decay for the whole memory, a per-channel rate so each feature fades at its own speed, then separate erase and write gates. Drag them apart.
- [hybrid-by-layer: interleaved SSM + periodic full attention](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/hybrid-by-layer/): Mostly recurrent layers with full attention every so often. Only the attention layers need a cache, so the memory cost falls in proportion to how few of them there are.

## F — CNN / vision

- [convolution: kernel sliding over input (stride / padding / dilation)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/convolution/): A kernel slides across the input and every output pixel is one sum of products. Stride, padding and dilation decide what it covers and how much the image shrinks.
- [receptive-field: how stacked convs grow what each output sees](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/receptive-field/): Stack convolutions and each output sees a wider slice of the input. Dilation widens that view faster without adding weights — the dependency cone, drawn layer by layer.
- [pooling: max / average pooling, downsampling](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/pooling/): A window collapses to a single number, by maximum or by average. Downsampling is cheap and lossy: watch which cell actually survived, and what was discarded to get there.
- [feature-maps: what a CNN sees: edges → textures → parts](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/feature-maps/): The channel activations of a convolutional stack layer by layer — edges, then textures, then parts. Paint on the input and watch which filters respond to what you drew.
- [batchnorm: running mean/variance + train vs inference](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/batchnorm/): Normalise each channel by its batch statistics, then scale and shift. Training uses the batch and inference uses a running average, and that mismatch is a classic source of bugs.
- [residual-block: the skip connection y = F(x) + x](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/residual-block/): A skip connection makes the block learn a correction instead of a replacement. That is what stops gradients vanishing with depth, and why very deep networks train at all.
- [depthwise-separable: MobileNet conv, the FLOP cut](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/depthwise-separable/): Split one convolution into a per-channel filter and a 1×1 mix. The full-conv cost over that split grows with the output count and stays under the kernel area.
- [patch-embedding: ViT: image → patches → tokens](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/patch-embedding/): An image cut into fixed squares, each flattened and projected into a token. It is exactly a strided convolution — and it is how a transformer comes to read pixels at all.

## G — Quantization / multimodal

- [quantization: fp16 → int4, group-wise](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/quantization/): Weights stored in four bits with a scale per group, then reconstructed on use. Watch the error against bit-width and group size, and watch one outlier ruin its whole group.
- [ternary weights: a multiply becomes an add](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ternary-weights/): Each weight rounds to −1, 0, or +1 and is stored with one scale. The reconstruction is that code times the scale. The readout sums the printed weights and the printed reconstructions.
- [structured sparsity: two nonzeros in every four](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/structured-sparsity/): Every group of four weights keeps the two largest magnitudes. A zero loses to any nonzero. Ties keep the earlier index. The dropped count is the nonzero count minus the count that stayed, so a group of zeros drops nothing.
- [vram-budget: where the GPU memory goes](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/vram-budget/): Live memory arithmetic: weights, cache, activations and overhead against a real card. Drag the context length and watch which term is the one that actually overflows.
- [multimodal-inject: vision/audio tokens in the text stream](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/multimodal-inject/): An encoder turns an image into vectors, a small projector reshapes them to token size, and they are spliced into the text sequence as though they had been typed.
- [vlm-connector: how the vision encoder reaches the language model](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/vlm-connector/): How a vision encoder’s patches actually become language-model tokens, and how many. Merge neighbours or resample to a fixed count — resolution is a token budget, not a quality dial.
- [rotation before quant: spread the spike](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/rotation-quant/): A rotation leaves the length of a vector unchanged and shrinks its largest entry. The same rotation has to hit the weight, or the product is a different one.

## H — End to end & training

- [forward-pass: one prompt → the next token, end to end](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/forward-pass/): One prompt to one next token through a small real transformer: tokenise, embed, attend, feed forward, project, sample. Step it and watch the residual stream change at each stage.
- [backprop: the backward pass (how a model learns)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/backprop/): Gradients flow backwards through a small graph by the chain rule. Switch on descent and watch the loss fall to zero — the whole of training, at a scale you can actually follow.
- [lora: a low-rank update instead of a full one](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/lora/): The update is the product of two thin matrices. Lower the rank and the stored count falls, while a full-rank change stays out of reach. Merged adapters add no serving multiply.
- [muon: orthogonalise the matrix update](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/muon/): A matrix gradient is orthogonalised so its singular values move toward one. Embeddings, the output head, and per-channel gains stay on a second optimizer.
- [activation recompute: memory against a second forward](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/activation-recompute/): Store every activation and spend the memory, or store none and pay a second forward. The combined cost has a minimum at a segment length in between.
- [training numerics: loss scale and master weights](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/training-numerics/): A loss scale lifts gradients into the narrow fp8 range. Too small and they flush. Too large and they overflow. The fp32 master copy is the memory price.
- [quantization-aware training: round in the forward, step the full weight](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/quantization-aware-training/): The forward pass rounds a high-precision weight onto a code and multiplies by the scale. The backward pass updates that high-precision weight as if the rounding derivative were 1, so the forward code stays put until a bin boundary.
- [distillation: the student copies the teacher](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/distillation/): A soft target is the teacher distribution. When the teacher prefers the wrong class, the student is trained to copy that error. Temperature spreads the mass back.

## I — Real-model grounding

- [real-embeddings: a trained model's semantic geometry](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-embeddings/): The default path embeds the words you type: load a trained model or stay on the labelled stand-in. The nested toggle draws constructed vectors whose leading prefix is the coarse part. Those vectors are not a truncation of the loaded model.
- [real-attention: finding GPT-2's heads (real weights)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-attention/): Real GPT-2 attention heads captured from a verified forward pass in the browser. Type a sentence and find the induction, previous-token and sink heads in the actual head map.
- [real-logits: what GPT-2 actually predicts next](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-logits/): The real next-token distribution from GPT-2 for a prefix you type, reshaped by temperature, top-k and top-p exactly as a sampler would. Checked against the reference implementation.
- [logit-lens: watching a prediction form across layers](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/logit-lens/): Apply the output head at every layer rather than only the last, and watch the prediction crystallise with depth. The early guesses are wrong in a way you can interpret.
- [real-neurons: which MLP units fire](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-neurons/): Which of a layer’s three thousand neurons fire for which tokens, from a real forward pass. This is the raw material of mechanistic interpretability rather than a diagram of it.
- [real-quant: int4 on actual GPT-2 weights](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-quant/): Quantise one real GPT-2 weight tensor: its true distribution, its outliers, and the error you actually get at each bit-width and group size. Only that tensor is fetched, not the model.
- [real-kv-cache: what fills up as GPT-2 generates](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-kv-cache/): Watch the real cache grow as GPT-2 generates: actual cached keys per layer and head, one fresh column per token, with the memory figure climbing alongside it.
- [real-generate: watch GPT-2 write (the capstone)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-generate/): A real GPT-2 writing text token by token in your browser, under greedy, temperature, top-k or top-p. Its greedy output matches the reference implementation exactly.
- [real-vision: a ViT classifying a real image](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/real-vision/): A real vision transformer classifying a real photograph in your browser: the image cut into patches, and the genuine top-five predictions that come back out of it.

## J — Serving-time mechanisms

- [paged-attention: a KV cache in blocks, not slabs](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/paged-attention/): The cache in fixed-size blocks with a per-sequence table, instead of one reserved slab. Watch the reserved-but-unused tails vanish, and two requests share one prompt’s blocks.
- [radix-attention: one KV cache shared across requests](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/radix-attention/): Prompts inserted into a shared tree, so a common system prompt is stored once. A new request reuses the longest matching prefix and computes only its own suffix.
- [kv fusion: reuse a chunk that is not a prefix](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-fusion/): A prefix tree reuses a chunk only when the request starts with it. Fusion keeps a later chunk and recomputes a fraction of its tokens, leaving a residual error on the rest.
- [RoPE splice: rotate a cached chunk to its new position](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/rope-splice/): A cached key still carries the position it was computed at. Rotating it by the gap to the new position makes the pairwise score match a key computed there.
- [unified radix: one match, three kinds of state](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/unified-radix/): One prefix match reuses full-attention KV for the whole match and sliding-window KV for only the tail that fits. A recurrent layer adds one checkpoint when the match exists, and with that layer off the checkpoint stays at zero.
- [kv fabric: one pool across machines](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-fabric/): A private cache hits only on the machine that stored the prefix. A shared pool hits when any machine has, so a repeat on a different machine is no longer a miss.
- [continuous-batching: refill the slot the moment a sequence stops](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/continuous-batching/): Static batching holds every slot until the longest sequence finishes; continuous batching refills a slot the moment it frees. Same arrivals, two schedulers, side by side.
- [chunked-prefill: splitting a prefill so it stops stalling everyone else](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/chunked-prefill/): A long prompt’s prefill split into budgeted chunks and interleaved with everyone else’s decoding. One knob, and it moves two different latencies in opposite directions.
- [speculative-decoding: draft k tokens, verify them in one pass](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/speculative-decoding/): A small model proposes several tokens and the large one checks them all in a single pass. Accepted tokens are nearly free — and a poor draft turns the whole thing into a loss.
- [windowed MTP: the draft does not read the whole context](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/windowed-mtp/): Draft heads read a sink plus a recent window, not the whole context. The target still checks every token, so a fact in the gap is accepted only at the blind rate.
- [block diffusion draft: a wider block, a weaker tail](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/block-diffusion/): A block drafter proposes several tokens at once. The first position is the sure one. Each later position is accepted less often, so a wider block has a weaker tail.
- [kv-eviction: a constant-size KV cache over a growing context](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-eviction/): A fixed memory budget under a growing context. A plain sliding window collapses; keeping the first couple of tokens rescues it almost entirely. Three policies, one score.
- [disaggregation: prefill pool, decode pool, KV cache on the wire](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/disaggregation/): Prefill and decode on separate machines, because the two phases want opposite hardware. The cache transfer between them is drawn on the critical path, where it can become a loss.
- [attention / expert split: a wire at every layer](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/attn-expert-split/): Attention and the experts on separate machines. KV crosses once and grows with context. Hidden states cross every layer and grow with the batch. The larger ship flips.
- [kv-quant: quantizing the KV cache, not the weights](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-quant/): Squeeze the conversation’s memory rather than the weights. Four bits with a scale per group — and a single outlier stretches its group’s scale and spoils all of its neighbours.
- [mla: Multi-head Latent Attention (cache one latent, not K and V per head)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/mla/): Cache one small shared summary per token instead of full keys and values per head, then rebuild the detail on use. The cache collapses; the per-step arithmetic grows to pay for it.
- [ring-attention: one sequence too long for any single device, attended to without any device ever holding all of it](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ring-attention/): One sequence sharded across devices, with cached keys rotating around a ring so every query eventually meets every key. Send the next block while computing the current one, or the ring stalls.
- [context-extension: running a rotary model past its trained context length](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/context-extension/): Pushing a model past its trained context. Interpolate every position and lose short-range resolution, or rescale only the slow dimensions whose full range was never seen. Both cost something.
- [constrained-decoding: a grammar as a bitmask over the vocabulary](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/constrained-decoding/): A grammar compiled into a per-step mask over the whole vocabulary, so an illegal token cannot be sampled at all. Runs of forced characters skip the model entirely.
- [parallelism: what actually crosses the wire when one model is split across GPUs](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/parallelism/): Tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallel move different bytes. KV-parallel attention gathers sequence shards of the cache only when more than one device is in the strip. Data-parallel attention still crosses nothing. The ring that passes keys or queries is a different page.
- [context-editing: compacting an agent transcript, and what the edit costs](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/context-editing/): Clearing old tool results from an agent’s history, which is cache eviction one layer up. The subtle cost: editing history invalidates the shared prefix everyone downstream was reusing.
- [prefix-routing: the load balancer that knows which replica holds your prefix](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/prefix-routing/): The load balancer that knows which replica already holds your prefix. Follow the cache too strictly and every request piles onto one machine while the others sit idle.
- [hybrid-cache-allocator: two memory shapes, one pool](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/hybrid-cache-allocator/): Two memory shapes in one pool: KV pages that grow with every token, and fixed state slabs claimed up front. One split cannot satisfy both — concurrency and context pull opposite ways.
- [batch-invariance: your reply depends on who else was batched with you](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/batch-invariance/): Adding numbers in a different order gives a different answer, and a GPU picks its order from the batch shape. Same prompt, same seed, different reply — because of who else was served.
- [kv-tiering: the cache spilled downhill, and the race on every hit](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/kv-tiering/): The cache spilled down to host memory and then to disk. On a later hit, fetch it back or rebuild it from the text — whichever is cheaper, and which one that is flips with depth and distance.
- [suffix-decoding: speculate from text you have already seen, with no draft model](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/suffix-decoding/): Two proposals with no draft model. Suffix mode copies a continuation the tree has seen; repetition lengthens that match and novel prose backs off to one token. Jacobi mode writes the last context token plus a position index even when the tree has no match, then keeps only the prefix the reference would emit. It does not copy a repeated n-gram.
- [context-parallelism: pass the KV, or pass the queries?](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/context-parallelism/): Given a sequence split across devices, move the cached keys or move the queries. Reading a full prompt makes moving the keys cheaper at every setting here. Writing the reply makes moving the queries cheaper only while that batch sits left of the crossing, and it does not when the KV shards persist.
- [ulysses: all heads become a full sequence on fewer heads](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ulysses/): One exchange gives each device the full sequence for a subset of heads. Attention on that slice matches single-device attention for those heads. A second exchange restores sequence sharding. A head count not divisible by the device count is refused.
- [dual-batch-overlap: hiding an expert all-to-all behind another microbatch](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/dual-batch-overlap/): Split the batch and interleave the halves so one half’s network transfer hides behind the other half’s arithmetic. Split too far and the pieces are too small to hide anything.

## K — Diffusion & generative

- [diffusion-noise: what a diffusion model is TRAINED to do](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/diffusion-noise/): Corrupt a sample by a known amount, then learn to predict what was added. The running guess of the clean image is blurry early because it is an average of everything it could be.
- [diffusion-sampler: integrating a learned field](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/diffusion-sampler/): Generation is integrating a path, and the step count is how coarsely you walk it — chosen at generation time, not trained in. Deterministic and stochastic, side by side.
- [guidance: classifier-free guidance: two predictions, then extrapolate](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/guidance/): Run the model with and without your prompt, then extrapolate away from the promptless answer. Adherence improves and then saturates, while variety collapses the whole way.
- [dit: a transformer over latent patches, conditioned by modulating the norm](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/dit/): The transformer that replaced the U-Net in image models. Its trick is that conditioning modulates the normalisation, with the gate starting at zero so each block begins as an identity.
- [latent-space: the compression that makes image generation affordable, and its ceiling](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/latent-space/): Generation runs in a compressed space, not in pixels, which is what makes it affordable. Whatever the encoder discards is gone before generation starts — a ceiling no sampling recovers.
- [few-step-distillation: changing the model so four steps are enough](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/few-step-distillation/): Training a student to jump most of a fifty-step path in one, which is why real-time generation exists. It is paid for in variety: hold the prompt, sweep the seed, watch outputs repeat.
- [self-forcing: a fast video model trained on its own frames](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/self-forcing/): A few-step video model trained on the teacher drifts, one step of error per frame. Trained on its own frames, every frame stays at that one-step error.
- [step cache: skip a small residual](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/teacache/): A sampler step whose residual is under the threshold is skipped, and the drift is the sum of those residuals. The skip count stays put between residuals and rises when the threshold passes the next one. One skip is a quarter of a four-step schedule.
- [video-time: time is just another axis you tokenize](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/video-time/): Time is one more axis to patch and compress. Drag the resolution, frame rate and clip length and watch tokens climb into the hundreds of thousands, with attention cost growing as the square.
- [audio-tokens: a waveform becomes a code stack (RVQ)](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/audio-tokens/): A waveform becomes a stack of codes: the first codebook carries the gist and each later one corrects what the previous missed. Drop the deepest and quality degrades instead of breaking.
- [ar-vs-diffusion-images: a sequence of tokens, or a canvas refined](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/ar-vs-diffusion-images/): Predict image patches one at a time like text, or refine the whole canvas at once. Two cost axes that genuinely disagree, so the page reports both and stages no winner.
- [diffusion language model: unmask the whole sequence, both directions](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/diffusion-lm/): Each step predicts every still-masked position under bidirectional attention. The masked count falls by one while any remain, and an empty mask stays empty. No causal cache is carried into the next step.

## L — Reasoning

- [thinking-tokens: the reasoning trace is a decoder setting](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/thinking-tokens/): Reasoning is ordinary generation between two literal tokens, so the decoder can steer it. Suppress the stop token and it keeps thinking; force it early and it must answer now.
- [pass-at-k: sharpening buys the first sample and sells the tail](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/pass-at-k/): Given one attempt the reinforcement-trained model wins. Given many, the original overtakes it — training sharpened what it will try rather than widening it, so the curves cross.
- [grpo-advantage: the group is the baseline](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/grpo-advantage/): Score a group of attempts, subtract the group’s own mean, and that is the learning signal — no value network. If every attempt agrees, every advantage is exactly zero and nothing is learned.
- [verifier-selection: three ways to spend the same test-time budget](https://viz.math.gaema.ai/verifier-selection/): Spend one budget three ways: keep the best-scored attempt, take the most common answer, or search stepwise. With an imperfect judge, keeping the best gets WORSE as you sample more.
